newsitem.title: UK: Man sees India end 96/97 sugar stocks at 7.7 mln t.
newsitem.headline: Man sees India end 96/97 sugar stocks at 7.7 mln t.

text.p: India is expected to finish its 1996/97 crop year with stocks totalling a massive 7.70 million tonnes of sugar in white value terms, trade house E D & F Man said on Tuesday.

At a current 7.9 million tonnes, the country's stocks were hanging "ominously over the market" and would be carried over into this season, it said in a monthly report. Despite a projected decline in production, India's estimated output of 15 million tonnes white value would still be the highest ever, helped by a cane output and area which were likely to be the third highest on record.
Sugar consumption was pegged at 13.7 million tonnes for 1996/97 and exports to reach 1.5 million tonnes, Man said.
Per capita consumption would grow at least at its present rate, which is almost half a kilogramme per year, it said.
